questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The main function of bulliform cells in grasses is :
options: to make the leaf impermeable to fungal spores.
to minimize water loss during water stress.
questions.solution:
Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless cells present on the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves.

When water is abundant, these cells absorb water, become turgid, and cause the leaf surface to be exposed.

During water stress, they lose turgor pressure and become flaccid, which makes the leaves curl inwards to minimize water loss.

Answer: to minimize water loss during water stress.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. Conjunctive tissueI. Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells
B. Casparian stripsII. Endodermal cells rich in starch
C. Subsidiary cellsIII. Tissue between xylem and phloem
D. Starch sheathIV. Endodermal cells with suberin deposition

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Conjunctive tissue is the parenchymatous tissue present between the xylem and phloem in roots.

Casparian strips are the water-impermeable, waxy suberin depositions present on the radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells.

Subsidiary cells are the specialised epidermal cells present in the vicinity of guard cells.

Starch sheath is the endodermis of a dicot stem, as its cells are rich in starch grains.

Thus, the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the incorrect statements from the following :
A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete.
B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms.
C. Pseudocoelom is possessed by Aschelminthes.
D. Notochord is persistent throughout life in the class Chondrichthyes.
E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.
Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system with a single opening that serves as both mouth and anus.

Statement B is incorrect. Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry, whereas their larvae exhibit bilateral symmetry.

Statement C is correct. Aschelminthes possess a pseudocoelom, where the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm but is present as scattered pouches.

Statement D is correct. In members of the class Chondrichthyes, the notochord is persistent throughout life.

Statement E is incorrect. Members of the class Reptilia are poikilotherms (cold-blooded) and cannot maintain a constant body temperature.

Therefore, the incorrect statements are B and E.

Answer: B and E only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. MolluscsI. Pulmonary respiration only
B. ReptilesII. Branchial respiration
C. Adult amphibiansIII. Cellular respiration
D. AmoebaIV. Pulmonary and Cutaneous respiration

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Molluscs primarily use gills for respiration, which is known as branchial respiration. Thus, A matches II.

Reptiles rely exclusively on lungs for gas exchange, which is termed pulmonary respiration. Thus, B matches I.

Adult amphibians, such as frogs, can respire through both their lungs and their moist skin, utilizing pulmonary and cutaneous respiration. Thus, C matches IV.

Amoeba is a unicellular organism that exchanges gases directly across its cell membrane via simple diffusion, which corresponds to cellular respiration. Thus, D matches III.

The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A group of researchers procured some fish-like animals and upon investigation the following characters were observed :
A. Endoskeleton was made of cartilage.
B. Ectoparasitic, as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth.
C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but $7$ pairs of gill slits were present.
Which of the following species of animals did they consider to fit best with these characters ?
questions.solution:
The given characteristics belong to the class Cyclostomata.

Members of this class are ectoparasites on some fishes. They have an elongated body bearing $6-15$ pairs of gill slits for respiration.

Cyclostomes have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.

Their body is devoid of scales and paired fins.

Cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.

Petromyzon (Lamprey) and Myxine (Hagfish) are examples of class Cyclostomata.

Scoliodon belongs to class Chondrichthyes.

Exocoetus belongs to class Osteichthyes.

Branchiostoma belongs to subphylum Cephalochordata.

Thus, Petromyzon sp. fits best with the given characters.

Answer: Petromyzon sp.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the set of fishes which belong to the class Osteichthyes :
options: Saw fish, Fighting fish and Dog fish
Flying fish, Angel fish and Fighting fish
questions.solution:
Flying fish (Exocoetus), Angel fish (Pterophyllum), and Fighting fish (Betta) are all bony fishes belonging to the class Osteichthyes.

Devil fish (Octopus) and Cuttlefish (Sepia) belong to the phylum Mollusca.

Hagfish (Myxine) belongs to the class Cyclostomata.

Saw fish (Pristis) and Dog fish (Scoliodon) belong to the class Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes).

Starfish (Asterias) belongs to the phylum Echinodermata.

Answer: Flying fish, Angel fish and Fighting fish

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The flightless bird with forelimbs modified as paddle-like structures suited for swimming is known as :
questions.solution:
Aptenodytes is the scientific name for the penguin.

Penguins are flightless birds that have their forelimbs modified into paddle-like flippers, which are highly adapted for swimming.

Struthio (ostrich) is flightless but adapted for running.

Neophron (vulture) and Psittacula (parrot) are flying birds.

Answer: Aptenodytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The main criteria used for Five Kingdom Classification proposed by R.H. Whittaker (1969) included :
A. Cell structure
B. Body organization
C. Presence of flagellum
D. Reproduction
E. Phylogenetic relationships
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, D and E only
questions.solution:
R.H. Whittaker (1969) proposed the Five Kingdom Classification. The main criteria used by him for this classification include:
1. Cell structure (prokaryotic or eukaryotic)
2. Body organisation (unicellular or multicellular)
3. Mode of nutrition (autotrophic or heterotrophic)
4. Reproduction
5. Phylogenetic relationships

Presence of flagellum was not used as a main criterion for the Five Kingdom Classification.

Therefore, the correct criteria from the given list are A, B, D, and E.

Answer: A, B, D and E only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Choose the correct statements regarding cell organelles and their inclusions.
A. The endomembrane system includes Golgi complex, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria.
B. Rough endoplasmic reticulum bears ribosomes on its surface.
C. Both mitochondria and plastids have circular DNA.
D. A network of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is called cytoskeleton.
E. Mitochondrion is a single membrane-bound structure.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because the endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Mitochondria are not part of the endomembrane system.

Statement B is correct because the rough endoplasmic reticulum bears ribosomes on its outer surface.

Statement C is correct because both mitochondria and plastids are semi-autonomous organelles that contain their own circular DNA.

Statement D is correct because the cytoskeleton is an elaborate network of proteinaceous structures, including microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments, present in the cytoplasm.

Statement E is incorrect because the mitochondrion is a double membrane-bound organelle, not single membrane-bound.

Therefore, statements B, C, and D are correct.

Answer: B, C and D only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Non-membrane bound cell organelles found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are :
questions.solution:
Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all living cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic.

Lysosomes are single membrane-bound organelles found only in eukaryotic cells.

Centrosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found only in animal cells, which are eukaryotic.

Mitochondria are double membrane-bound organelles found only in eukaryotic cells.

Answer: Ribosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis ?
questions.solution:
The nucleolus is a dense, non-membrane bound structure located within the nucleus.

It is the primary site for the transcription and processing of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and the assembly of ribosomes.

Cells that are actively engaged in protein synthesis typically have larger and more numerous nucleoli.

Answer: Nucleolus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the correct statements regarding cell membrane in eukaryotic cell.
A. Membrane of human RBCs has approximately $52\%$ protein.
B. Major phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer.
C. Extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell form mesosomes.
D. Tails towards the inner part of lipids are hydrophobic and thus protected from aqueous medium.
E. Glycocalyx is present on the outer surface of the plasma membrane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. Chemical studies on human red blood cells (RBCs) show that the cell membrane consists of approximately $52\%$ protein and $40\%$ lipids.

Statement B is correct. The cell membrane is mainly composed of lipids, primarily phospholipids, which are arranged in a bilayer.

Statement C is incorrect. Mesosomes are formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell in prokaryotes, not in eukaryotic cells.

Statement D is correct. The lipids are arranged within the membrane with the polar hydrophilic heads towards the outer sides and the non-polar hydrophobic tails towards the inner part, ensuring that the non-polar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.

Since statement C is incorrect for eukaryotic cells, any option containing C is eliminated. Thus, statements A, B, and D are the correct choices.

Answer: A, B and D only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Phase of cell cycle)List II (Activity)
A. $G_1$ phaseI. Actual cell division occurs
B. S phaseII. Cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA
C. $G_2$ phaseIII. Synthesis of DNA occurs and the amount of DNA per cell doubles
D. M phaseIV. Proteins are synthesized while cell growth continues

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
In the $G_1$ phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.

In the S phase (synthesis phase), DNA replication takes place and the amount of DNA per cell doubles.

In the $G_2$ phase, proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

In the M phase, actual cell division or mitosis occurs.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

Answer: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. ProductivityI. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses
B. Net primary productivityII. Rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
C. Gross primary productivityIII. Rate of biomass production
D. Secondary productivityIV. Rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Productivity is defined as the rate of biomass production.

Gross primary productivity (GPP) of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.

Net primary productivity (NPP) is the gross primary productivity minus respiration losses ($R$), which is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs.

Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ecological pyramids represent the relationship between the organisms at different trophic levels and they are generally inverted for :
options: Pyramid of energy in pond ecosystem
questions.solution:
The pyramid of biomass in a sea or aquatic ecosystem is generally inverted because the biomass of fishes (primary and secondary consumers) far exceeds that of phytoplankton (producers).

The pyramid of number in a grassland is upright.

The pyramid of energy is always upright in all ecosystems because energy is lost as heat at each trophic level.

The pyramid of biomass in a grassland is upright.

Answer: Pyramid of biomass in sea

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. DecompositionI. Accumulation of dark coloured amorphous colloidal substance
B. DetritusII. Release of inorganic nutrients by the activity of microbes in soil
C. MineralisationIII. Breaking down of complex organic matter into inorganic substances
D. HumificationIV. Dead remains of plants and animals including faecal matter

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Decomposition is the process of breaking down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water, and nutrients.

Detritus constitutes the dead remains of plants and animals, including faecal matter, which serves as the raw material for decomposition.

Mineralisation is the process by which microbes further degrade humus to release inorganic nutrients into the soil.

Humification leads to the accumulation of a dark-coloured, amorphous, colloidal substance called humus, which is highly resistant to microbial action.

Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In racemose inflorescence, ____________.
options: the main axis terminates in a flower
flowers are borne in an acropetal succession
questions.solution:
In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow indefinitely and does not terminate in a flower. The flowers are borne laterally in an acropetal succession, meaning the older flowers are at the base and the younger flowers or buds are at the apex.

In cymose inflorescence, the main axis terminates in a flower, hence its growth is limited, and the flowers are borne in a basipetal order.

Answer: flowers are borne in an acropetal succession

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Placentation)List II (Example)
A. MarginalI. Mustard
B. AxileII. Pea
C. ParietalIII. Marigold
D. BasalIV. Lemon

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Marginal placentation is found in pea where the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary.

Axile placentation is found in lemon, tomato, and china rose where the placenta is axial and ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary.

Parietal placentation is found in mustard and argemone where ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary.

Basal placentation is found in marigold and sunflower where the placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it.

Thus, A matches II, B matches IV, C matches I, and D matches III.

Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In angiosperms, root hairs arise from which one of the following regions of the root ?
questions.solution:
The root is divided into different regions from the apex to the base: the root cap, the region of meristematic activity, the region of elongation, and the region of maturation.

The cells of the elongation zone gradually differentiate and mature to form the region of maturation. From the epidermal cells of the region of maturation, very fine and delicate, thread-like structures called root hairs arise.

These root hairs significantly increase the surface area for the absorption of water and minerals from the soil.

Answer: The region of maturation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following floral formula is the correct floral formula of Solanaceae family ?
questions.solution:
The Solanaceae family exhibits the following floral characteristics:

- Symmetry: Actinomorphic, represented by $\oplus$.
- Sexuality: Bisexual.
- Calyx: 5 sepals that are united (gamosepalous), represented by $\text{K}_{(5)}$.
- Corolla: 5 petals that are united (gamopetalous), represented by $\text{C}_{(5)}$.
- Androecium: 5 stamens that are epipetalous (attached to the petals). This is represented by an arc connecting the corolla and androecium symbols: $\widehat{\text{C}_{(5)} \text{A}_{5}}$.
- Gynoecium: Bicarpellary, syncarpous, with a superior ovary, represented by $\underline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$.

Comparing these features with the given options, Formula (2) correctly displays all these characteristics. Formula (1) is incorrect as it lacks the arc indicating the epipetalous condition. Formulas (3) and (4) are incorrect because they show free sepals or petals (lacking parentheses).

Answer: Formula (2)
questions._originalQ: Which of the following floral formula is the correct floral formula of Solanaceae family ?

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many ATP and NADPH molecules are required to make one molecule of glucose through the Calvin pathway ?
questions.solution:
In the Calvin cycle, the fixation of one molecule of $CO_2$ requires $3$ ATP and $2$ NADPH molecules.

To synthesize one molecule of glucose, $6$ molecules of $CO_2$ must be fixed.

Total ATP required = $6 \times 3 = 18$ ATP.

Total NADPH required = $6 \times 2 = 12$ NADPH.

Answer: $18$ ATP and $12$ NADPH

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Find the incorrect statement(s) about photosynthesis from the following :
A. The water splitting complex is associated with PS I.
B. $\text{C}_4$ plants use the $\text{C}_3$ pathway of $\text{CO}_2$ fixation as the main biosynthetic pathway.
C. In $\text{C}_4$ plants, photorespiration does not occur.
D. $\text{C}_3$ plants exhibit 'Kranz' anatomy.
E. ATP synthesis in chloroplast occurs through chemiosmosis.
Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because the water splitting complex is associated with PS II, not PS I.

Statement B is correct because the Calvin cycle ($\text{C}_3$ pathway) is the main biosynthetic pathway for all plants, including $\text{C}_4$ plants.

Statement C is correct because $\text{C}_4$ plants have a mechanism that increases the concentration of $\text{CO}_2$ at the enzyme site, preventing RuBisCO from acting as an oxygenase, thus avoiding photorespiration.

Statement D is incorrect because Kranz anatomy is a characteristic feature of $\text{C}_4$ plants, not $\text{C}_3$ plants.

Statement E is correct because ATP synthesis in chloroplasts is explained by the chemiosmotic hypothesis.

Therefore, the incorrect statements are A and D.

Answer: A and D only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The enzyme required for carboxylation in the Calvin cycle is :
questions.solution:
The Calvin cycle is the primary pathway for carbon fixation in plants.

The first step of the Calvin cycle is carboxylation, where carbon dioxide is added to a five-carbon acceptor molecule, Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP).

This reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase, commonly known as RuBisCO.

Hexokinase is an enzyme involved in glycolysis.

PEP carboxylase is the primary carboxylating enzyme in the C4 pathway.

Carboxypeptidase is a proteolytic enzyme involved in digestion.

Answer: RuBP carboxylase – oxygenase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Heterophyllous development in response to environment is an example of which of the following phenomena ?
questions.solution:
Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity.

Heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur is an example of plasticity in response to phases of life, whereas heterophylly in buttercup is an example of plasticity in response to the environment. In buttercup, the leaves of juvenile plants and mature plants are different in shape, and similarly, the leaves of submerged plants are highly dissected compared to the broad leaves of aerial plants.

Answer: Plasticity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of plant cells in the phase of elongation ?
questions.solution:
The period of growth is generally divided into three phases: meristematic, elongation, and maturation.

The cells in the meristematic phase are rich in protoplasm and possess large conspicuous nuclei. Their cell walls are primary in nature, thin, and cellulosic with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

The cells in the phase of elongation are characterised by increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition.

Therefore, large conspicuous nuclei are a characteristic of meristematic cells, not cells in the phase of elongation.

Answer: Large conspicuous nuclei

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Growth Regulator)List II (Function/Effect)
A. $2,4$-DI. Brewing industry
B. $\text{GA}_3$II. Stimulation of stomatal closure
C. KinetinIII. Herbicide
D. ABAIV. Nutrient mobilisation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$2,4$-D is a synthetic auxin widely used as a herbicide to kill broad-leaved dicot weeds.

$\text{GA}_3$ (Gibberellic acid) is used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.

Kinetin is a cytokinin that promotes nutrient mobilisation, which helps in the delay of leaf senescence.

ABA (Abscisic acid) acts as a stress hormone and stimulates the closure of stomata under conditions of water stress.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which one of the following, the ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall and remain exposed ?
questions.solution:
Gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization.

Pinus is a gymnosperm, so its ovules are naked and remain exposed.

Funaria is a bryophyte and Selaginella is a pteridophyte, both of which do not produce ovules or seeds.

Wolffia is an angiosperm, in which the ovules are enclosed within an ovary wall.

Answer: Pinus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
$2\ (\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{C}_6) + 145\ \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 102\ \text{CO}_2 + 98\ \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{energy}$
The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of a biomolecule, used for respiration, as per the above equation would be :
questions.solution:
The respiratory quotient (RQ) is defined as the ratio of the volume of carbon dioxide evolved to the volume of oxygen consumed during respiration.

From the given balanced chemical equation:
Volume of $\text{CO}_2$ evolved $= 102$
Volume of $\text{O}_2$ consumed $= 145$

$\text{RQ} = \dfrac{102}{145} \approx 0.7$

The calculated value of RQ is approximately $0.7$, which lies between $0.5$ and $0.95$.

Answer: Between $0.5$ and $0.95$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Process)List II (Location)
A. GlycolysisI. Inner mitochondrial membrane
B. ETSII. Mitochondrial matrix
C. Accumulation of protonsIII. Cytoplasm
D. Krebs' cycleIV. Intermembrane space

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Glycolysis is the first step of cellular respiration and occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell.

The Electron Transport System (ETS) is located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

During ETS, protons are pumped from the mitochondrial matrix to the intermembrane space, leading to the accumulation of protons in the intermembrane space.

The Krebs' cycle (TCA cycle) takes place in the mitochondrial matrix.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the following in the correct development sequence related to microsporogenesis :
A. Microspore tetrads
B. Sporogenous tissue
C. Pollen grains
D. Pollen mother cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
During the development of an anther, the cells of the sporogenous tissue undergo meiotic divisions to form microspore tetrads. Each cell of the sporogenous tissue acts as a pollen mother cell (PMC). The PMCs undergo meiosis to form microspore tetrads. As the anthers mature and dehydrate, the microspores dissociate from each other and develop into pollen grains.

The correct developmental sequence is:
Sporogenous tissue \rightarrow Pollen mother cells \rightarrow Microspore tetrads \rightarrow Pollen grains.

This corresponds to the sequence B, D, A, C.

Answer: B, D, A, C

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following types of pollination brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma ?
questions.solution:
Autogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower, resulting in genetically identical offspring.

Geitonogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. Although it is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, it is genetically similar to autogamy since the pollen grains come from the same plant.

Cleistogamy occurs in closed flowers which do not open at all, ensuring strict autogamy.

Xenogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a different plant. This is the only type of pollination which during pollination brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma.

Answer: Xenogamy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is a triploid cell ?
questions.solution:
Synergids are haploid ($n$) cells present in the embryo sac.

The central cell contains two polar nuclei ($n + n$) which fuse to form a diploid secondary nucleus ($2n$).

The zygote is a diploid ($2n$) cell formed by the fusion of a male gamete ($n$) with the egg cell ($n$).

The primary endosperm cell is formed by the fusion of a male gamete ($n$) with the two polar nuclei or secondary nucleus ($2n$) of the central cell. This process is called triple fusion, resulting in a triploid ($3n$) primary endosperm cell.

Answer: Primary endosperm cell

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is not true about the universal rules of binomial nomenclature ?
options: Biological names are generally in Latin.
Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined or printed in italics.
The specific epithet in the biological name starts with a small letter.
The first word in the biological name represents the specific epithet, while the second component denotes the genus.
questions.solution:
According to the universal rules of binomial nomenclature, the first word in a biological name represents the genus, while the second component denotes the specific epithet.

Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. They are Latinised or derived from Latin irrespective of their origin.

Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin.

The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.

Answer: The first word in the biological name represents the specific epithet, while the second component denotes the genus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines :
A. (i) $\text{LiAlH}_4$; (ii) $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
B. $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$
C. $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$
D. $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$
E. $\text{Br}_2/\text{aq. NaOH}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Nitriles ($R-CN$) can be reduced to primary amines ($R-CH_2NH_2$) using strong reducing agents or catalytic hydrogenation.

Reagent A: $\text{LiAlH}_4$ followed by hydrolysis is a strong reducing agent that reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent C: $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$ (catalytic hydrogenation) reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent D: $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ (Mendius reduction) provides nascent hydrogen and reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent B: $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$ is typically used to reduce nitro compounds to amines. (Note: $\text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl}$ is used in Stephen reduction to convert nitriles to aldehydes).

Reagent E: $\text{Br}_2/\text{aq. NaOH}$ is used for Hoffmann bromamide degradation to convert amides to primary amines, not nitriles.

Thus, A, C, and D are the correct reagents.

Answer: A, C and D only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The major product Z formed in the following sequence of reactions is :
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow[\text{UV light}]{\text{Cl}_2} X \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3} Y \xrightarrow[(\text{monochlorinated product})]{\text{(i) NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}\ \ \text{(ii) H}_2\text{O}} Z$
questions.solution:
Ethane undergoes free radical halogenation with chlorine in the presence of UV light to form ethyl chloride (X).

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV light}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \ (X)$

Ethyl chloride reacts with ammonia via nucleophilic substitution to form ethylamine (Y).

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \ (Y)$

Ethylamine, being a primary aliphatic amine, reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}$) to form an unstable aliphatic diazonium salt, which decomposes to yield a carbocation. The carbocation reacts with water to form ethanol (Z).

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} [\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^{+}\text{Cl}^{-}] \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \ (Z) + \text{N}_2 + \text{HCl}$

Thus, the major product Z is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements about biomolecules.
A. Lipids are generally water soluble.
B. Proteins are polypeptides.
C. Polysaccharides are long chains of sugars.
D. Adenine and guanine are substituted pyrimidines.
E. Almost all enzymes are proteins.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because lipids are generally water insoluble.

Statement B is correct because proteins are polypeptides, which are linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.

Statement C is correct because polysaccharides are long chains of sugars (monosaccharides).

Statement D is incorrect because adenine and guanine are substituted purines, whereas cytosine, uracil, and thymine are substituted pyrimidines.

Statement E is correct because almost all enzymes are proteins, with a few exceptions like ribozymes (which are nucleic acids).

Therefore, the correct statements are B, C, and E.

Answer: B, C and E only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct statement with regard to the secondary structure of DNA/RNA is :
options: RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.
DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.
RNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases.
DNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases.
questions.solution:
DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine as its four bases.

RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and uracil as its four bases.

Thus, the statement that DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases is correct.

Answer: DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding amino acids ?
A. They are substituted methanes.
B. Serine is an aromatic amino acid.
C. Valine is a neutral amino acid.
D. Lysine is an acidic amino acid.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Amino acids are organic compounds containing an amino group and an acidic group as substituents on the same carbon, i.e., the $\alpha$-carbon. Therefore, they are considered substituted methanes. Statement A is correct.

Serine contains a hydroxymethyl group ($\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$) as its side chain and is an aliphatic amino acid, not an aromatic one. Aromatic amino acids include phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan. Statement B is incorrect.

Valine contains one amino group and one carboxyl group, making it a neutral amino acid. Statement C is correct.

Lysine contains two amino groups and one carboxyl group, making it a basic amino acid, not an acidic one. Acidic amino acids include aspartic acid and glutamic acid. Statement D is incorrect.

Thus, only statements A and C are correct.

Answer: A and C only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Alpha-helix is found in which level of protein structure ?
questions.solution:
The primary structure of a protein refers to the linear sequence of amino acids.

The secondary structure refers to the local folded structures that form within a polypeptide due to interactions between atoms of the backbone. The most common types of secondary structures are the $\alpha$-helix and the $\beta$-pleated sheet.

The tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional structure of a polypeptide.

The quaternary structure is the arrangement of multiple folded protein or coiling protein molecules in a multi-subunit complex.

Therefore, the $\alpha$-helix is found in the secondary structure of proteins.

Answer: Secondary structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered $2$, $1$ and $3$ respectively are :
questions.solution:
The formal charge (FC) on an atom in a Lewis structure is given by the formula:

$FC = V - L - \dfrac{S}{2}$

where $V$ is the number of valence electrons, $L$ is the number of non-bonding electrons, and $S$ is the number of shared (bonding) electrons.

For oxygen, the number of valence electrons is $V = 6$.

For oxygen atom $1$ (central atom):
It has $1$ lone pair ($2$ non-bonding electrons) and $3$ bonds ($6$ shared electrons).
$FC_{1} = 6 - 2 - \dfrac{6}{2} = +1$

For oxygen atom $2$ (left atom):
It has $2$ lone pairs ($4$ non-bonding electrons) and $2$ bonds ($4$ shared electrons).
$FC_{2} = 6 - 4 - \dfrac{4}{2} = 0$

For oxygen atom $3$ (right atom):
It has $3$ lone pairs ($6$ non-bonding electrons) and $1$ bond ($2$ shared electrons).
$FC_{3} = 6 - 6 - \dfrac{2}{2} = -1$

The formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered $2$, $1$, and $3$ respectively are $0, +1, -1$.

Answer: $0, +1, -1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$I. $3\ \sigma$ bonds, $2\ \pi$ bonds
B. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$II. $3\ \sigma$ bonds, one lone pair
C. $\text{CH}_4$III. $4\ \sigma$ bonds
D. $\text{NH}_3$IV. $5\ \sigma$ bonds, $1\ \pi$ bond

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
For $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (Ethene), the structure is $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$. It contains $4\text{C}-\text{H}$ single bonds and $1\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond. A single bond is a $\sigma$ bond, and a double bond consists of $1\sigma$ and $1\pi$ bond. Total bonds: $5\ \sigma$ bonds and $1\ \pi$ bond. Thus, A matches IV.

For $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ (Ethyne), the structure is $\text{HC}\equiv\text{CH}$. It contains $2\text{C}-\text{H}$ single bonds and $1\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ triple bond. A triple bond consists of $1\sigma$ and $2\pi$ bonds. Total bonds: $3\ \sigma$ bonds and $2\ \pi$ bonds. Thus, B matches I.

For $\text{CH}_4$ (Methane), the central carbon atom is bonded to $4$ hydrogen atoms via single bonds. Total bonds: $4\ \sigma$ bonds. Thus, C matches III.

For $\text{NH}_3$ (Ammonia), the central nitrogen atom is bonded to $3$ hydrogen atoms via single bonds and has $1$ lone pair of electrons. Total bonds: $3\ \sigma$ bonds and one lone pair. Thus, D matches II.

The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement about $\text{ClF}_3$ from the following options :
options: It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a planar trigonal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
questions.solution:
The central atom in $\text{ClF}_3$ is Chlorine (Cl).

Number of valence electrons of Cl = $7$.

Number of monovalent atoms (F) attached = $3$.

Steric number = $\dfrac{1}{2}(7 + 3) = 5$.

The hybridization of the central atom is $sp^3d$.

Number of bond pairs = $3$.

Number of lone pairs = $5 - 3 = 2$.

The electron geometry is trigonal bipyramidal. According to VSEPR theory, to minimize repulsion, the two lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions.

This results in a T-shaped molecular geometry.

Therefore, $\text{ClF}_3$ has a T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on the Cl atom.

Answer: It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given below are certain reactions. Identify the reaction for which $K_p \neq K_c$ :
questions.solution:
The relation between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is given by $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$, where $\Delta n_g$ is the difference between the number of moles of gaseous products and gaseous reactants.

For $K_p \neq K_c$, $\Delta n_g$ must be non-zero.

For $\text{H}_2\text{O (g)} + \text{CO (g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow K_p = K_c$

For $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2 \Rightarrow K_p \neq K_c$

For $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI (g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow K_p = K_c$

For $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO (g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow K_p = K_c$

Answer: $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Order of reaction)List II (Unit of rate constant)
A. Zero orderI. $\text{mol}^{-1}\ \text{L}\ \text{s}^{-1}$
B. First orderII. $\text{mol}^{-2}\ \text{L}^{2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$
C. Second orderIII. $\text{s}^{-1}$
D. Third orderIV. $\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The unit of rate constant $k$ for an $n$-th order reaction is given by $(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-n}\ \text{s}^{-1}$.

For zero order reaction ($n=0$):
Unit $= (\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-0}\ \text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ (Matches A with IV)

For first order reaction ($n=1$):
Unit $= (\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-1}\ \text{s}^{-1} = \text{s}^{-1}$ (Matches B with III)

For second order reaction ($n=2$):
Unit $= (\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-2}\ \text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}^{-1}\ \text{L}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ (Matches C with I)

For third order reaction ($n=3$):
Unit $= (\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-3}\ \text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}^{-2}\ \text{L}^{2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ (Matches D with II)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, $T$ (K).
$\ln k = 14.34 - \dfrac{1.25 \times 10^{4}}{T}$
The energy of activation in kcal mol$^{-1}$ for the reaction is :
(Given : $k$ in s$^{-1}$, $R = 1.987$ cal mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The Arrhenius equation is given by:

$\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$

The given equation is:

$\ln k = 14.34 - \dfrac{1.25 \times 10^{4}}{T}$

Comparing the two equations:

$\dfrac{E_a}{R} = 1.25 \times 10^{4}$

$E_a = 1.25 \times 10^{4} \times R$

Substituting $R = 1.987$ cal mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$:

$E_a = 1.25 \times 10^{4} \times 1.987$

$E_a = 24837.5$ cal mol$^{-1}$

$E_a = 24.8375$ kcal mol$^{-1} \approx 24.84$ kcal mol$^{-1}$

Answer: $24.84$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction $R \rightarrow$ Product, the plot of concentration $[R]$ vs time has a negative slope as shown. The order of reaction is :
questions.solution:
From the given graph, the plot of concentration $[R]$ versus time $t$ is a straight line with a negative slope.

The equation for this straight line can be written as:
$y = mx + c$
$[R] = (\text{slope}) \times t + \text{intercept}$

Given that the intercept is $[R_0]$ and the slope is $-k$, the equation becomes:
$[R] = -kt + [R_0]$

This equation represents the integrated rate law for a zero-order reaction. For a zero-order reaction, the rate of reaction is independent of the concentration of the reactant:
$\text{Rate} = -\dfrac{d[R]}{dt} = k[R]^0 = k$

Integrating both sides:
$\int_{[R_0]}^{[R]} d[R] = -k \int_0^t dt$
$[R] - [R_0] = -kt$
$[R] = -kt + [R_0]$

Since the graph matches this equation, the order of the reaction is $0$.

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
options: The largest and the smallest species among Mg, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, Al and $\text{Al}^{3+}$ are Al and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, respectively.
The IUPAC name of the element with atomic number $107$ is Unnilseptium.
The similarity in behaviour of Li with Mg is referred to as 'diagonal relationship'.
The oxidation state and covalency of Al in $[\text{AlCl}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5]^{2+}$ are $3$ and $6$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Atomic radius decreases across a period from left to right, so the atomic radius of $\text{Mg}$ is greater than that of $\text{Al}$.

For isoelectronic species, the ionic radius decreases with an increase in nuclear charge. Both $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Al}^{3+}$ have $10$ electrons, but $\text{Al}^{3+}$ has a higher nuclear charge ($Z=13$) compared to $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ($Z=12$), making $\text{Al}^{3+}$ smaller than $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.

Cations are always smaller than their respective parent atoms. Therefore, the overall decreasing order of size is $\text{Mg} \gt \text{Al} \gt \text{Mg}^{2+} \gt \text{Al}^{3+}$. The largest species is $\text{Mg}$ and the smallest is $\text{Al}^{3+}$. Thus, statement (1) is incorrect.

For atomic number $107$, the IUPAC roots are un ($1$), nil ($0$), and sept ($7$), giving the name Unnilseptium. Statement (2) is correct.

Lithium and Magnesium exhibit similar properties due to their comparable polarizing power (charge-to-size ratio), which is known as a diagonal relationship. Statement (3) is correct.

In the complex $[\text{AlCl}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5]^{2+}$, let the oxidation state of $\text{Al}$ be $x$. We have $x + (-1) + 5(0) = +2 \Rightarrow x = +3$. The central metal atom is surrounded by $6$ ligands ($1$ chloride and $5$ water molecules), so its covalency is $6$. Statement (4) is correct.

Answer: The largest and the smallest species among Mg, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, Al and $\text{Al}^{3+}$ are Al and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The correct order of increasing metallic character of Na, Be, P, Mg and Si is :
questions.solution:
Metallic character is the tendency of an element to lose electrons. It decreases across a period from left to right and increases down a group.

The elements $\text{Na}$, $\text{Mg}$, $\text{Si}$, and $\text{P}$ belong to the third period. Across a period, metallic character decreases, so the order is $\text{Na} \gt \text{Mg} \gt \text{Si} \gt \text{P}$.

The elements $\text{Be}$ and $\text{Mg}$ belong to Group 2. Down a group, metallic character increases, so $\text{Mg} \gt \text{Be}$.

Comparing $\text{Be}$ (a metal) with $\text{Si}$ (a metalloid) and $\text{P}$ (a non-metal), $\text{Be}$ is more metallic than both $\text{Si}$ and $\text{P}$.

Combining these observations, the increasing order of metallic character is $\text{P} \lt \text{Si} \lt \text{Be} \lt \text{Mg} \lt \text{Na}$.

Answer: $P \lt Si \lt Be \lt Mg \lt Na$

For $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$, Fe is in $0$ oxidation state. With a coordination number of 5, it forms a trigonal bipyramidal geometry with $dsp^3$ hybridization.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $MA_2B_2$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms).

B. $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$ is an octahedral complex with three symmetrical bidentate ligands. It lacks a plane of symmetry and exhibits optical isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is an ambidentate ligand ?
questions.solution:
An ambidentate ligand is a unidentate ligand that has more than one donor atom but coordinates to the central metal atom or ion through only one donor atom at a time.

Thiocyanate ion ($SCN^{-}$ or $NCS^{-}$) has two donor atoms, sulfur ($S$) and nitrogen ($N$). It can bind to the metal through either the sulfur atom (thiocyanato) or the nitrogen atom (isothiocyanato). Thus, it is an ambidentate ligand.

Ethane-$1,2$-diamine is a bidentate ligand.

Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion is a hexadentate ligand.

Oxalate is a bidentate ligand.

Answer: Thiocyanate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Although $+3$ oxidation state is most common in lanthanoids, cerium still shows $+4$ oxidation state because :
options: After losing one more electron, it acquires $4f^{14}$ electronic configuration.
Its nearest inert gas is Radon.
After losing one more electron, it acquires $4f^{0}$ electronic configuration.
questions.solution:
The atomic number of Cerium (Ce) is $58$.

The electronic configuration of Ce is $[Xe] 4f^{1} 5d^{1} 6s^{2}$.

In $+3$ oxidation state, the electronic configuration of $Ce^{3+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{1}$.

By losing one more electron, it forms $Ce^{4+}$ ion.

The electronic configuration of $Ce^{4+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{0}$, which is a highly stable noble gas configuration.

Thus, Cerium shows $+4$ oxidation state because after losing one more electron from $+3$ state, it acquires $4f^{0}$ electronic configuration.

Answer: After losing one more electron, it acquires $4f^{0}$ electronic configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of $\text{Ti}^{2+}\ (3d^2)$ is :
questions.solution:
The atomic number of $\text{Ti}$ is $22$.

Electronic configuration of $\text{Ti}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^2 4s^2$.

Electronic configuration of $\text{Ti}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^2$.

Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 2$.

Spin-only magnetic moment, $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

$\mu = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.84 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $2.84$ BM

A. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$I. Preparation of ammonia from $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$ mixture
B. $\text{Fe}$II. Polymerisation of alkynes
C. $\text{PdCl}_2$III. Preparation of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ from $\text{SO}_2$
D. Ni complexIV. Oxidation of ethyne to ethanal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

$\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is used as a catalyst in the Contact process for the oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ during the preparation of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Thus, A matches with III.

Finely divided $\text{Fe}$ is used as a catalyst in the Haber process for the preparation of ammonia from $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{H}_2$ mixture. Thus, B matches with I.

$\text{PdCl}_2$ is used as a catalyst in the Wacker process for the oxidation of ethene (referred to as ethyne in the given options) to ethanal. Thus, C matches with IV.

$\text{Ni}$ complexes are used as catalysts for the polymerisation of alkynes (e.g., polymerisation of ethyne to cyclooctatetraene). Thus, D matches with II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed for $10$ minutes with a current of $1.5$ amperes. The mass of copper deposited at cathode is :
(Given : Molar mass of $\text{Cu} = 63$ g mol$^{-1}$; $1$ F $= 96487$ C mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The reaction at the cathode is $\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^{-} \rightarrow \text{Cu}$.

The quantity of charge $Q$ passed through the solution is given by $Q = I \times t$.

Substituting the given values:
$Q = 1.5 \text{ A} \times (10 \times 60) \text{ s} = 900 \text{ C}$

From Faraday's first law of electrolysis, the mass of copper deposited is:
$m = \dfrac{M \times Q}{n \times F}$

Here, $M = 63 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $n = 2$, and $F = 96487 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$.

$m = \dfrac{63 \times 900}{2 \times 96487}$

$m = \dfrac{56700}{192974} \approx 0.2938 \text{ g}$

Answer: $0.2938$ g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate emf of the half cell given below :
$\text{Pt (s)} | \text{H}_2 \text{(g, 2 atm)} | \text{HCl (aq, 0.02 M)}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^{+}} = 0$ V
$\left(\text{Given}: \dfrac{2.303\ RT}{F} = 0.059, \log 2 = 0.3010\right)$
questions.solution:
The given half-cell is represented as an oxidation electrode: $\text{Pt (s)} | \text{H}_2 \text{(g)} | \text{H}^{+} \text{(aq)}$.

The corresponding oxidation half-cell reaction is:
$\text{H}_2 \text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}^{+} \text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^{-}$

Using the Nernst equation for the oxidation potential:
$E = E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^{+}} - \dfrac{0.059}{n} \log \dfrac{[\text{H}^{+}]^2}{P_{\text{H}_2}}$

Given values:
$E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^{+}} = 0$ V
$n = 2$
$[\text{H}^{+}] = 0.02$ M (since HCl is a strong monoprotic acid)
$P_{\text{H}_2} = 2$ atm

Substituting the values into the Nernst equation:
$E = 0 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \log \dfrac{(0.02)^2}{2}$

$E = -0.0295 \log \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-4}}{2}$

$E = -0.0295 \log (2 \times 10^{-4})$

$E = -0.0295 (\log 2 + \log 10^{-4})$

$E = -0.0295 (0.3010 - 4)$

$E = -0.0295 \times (-3.699)$

$E = 0.10912$ V $\approx 0.109$ V

Answer: $0.109$ V

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pair of molecules that are metamers among the following is :
questions.solution:
Metamerism is a type of structural isomerism where isomers have the same molecular formula but differ in the nature of the alkyl groups attached to the same polyvalent functional group (such as $-\text{O}-$, $-\text{S}-$, $-\text{NH}-$, $-\text{CO}-$).

In option (1), $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3$ are position isomers because the position of the $-\text{OH}$ group differs.

In option (2), $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ are chain isomers because the carbon skeleton differs.

In option (3), $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$ are functional isomers because they have different functional groups (ketone and aldehyde).

In option (4), $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (methoxypropane) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (ethoxyethane) have the same polyvalent functional group ($-\text{O}-$) but different alkyl groups attached to it (methyl and propyl versus two ethyl groups). Thus, they are metamers.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During Lassaigne's test, the elements present in an organic compound are converted from :
questions.solution:
In Lassaigne's test, an organic compound is fused with sodium metal. The elements present in the organic compound, such as nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens, are initially present in covalent form.

During the fusion process, these elements react with sodium to form ionic sodium salts. For example, nitrogen and carbon form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), sulphur forms sodium sulphide ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}$), and halogens form sodium halides ($\text{NaX}$).

Therefore, the elements are converted from covalent form to ionic form.

Answer: covalent form to ionic form

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is :
questions.solution:
1. Identify the longest continuous carbon chain: The longest chain in the given structure contains $7$ carbon atoms. Therefore, the parent alkane is heptane.

2. Identify the substituents: There is an ethyl group ($\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) and a methyl group ($\text{-CH}_3$) attached to the main chain.

3. Number the carbon chain:
- Numbering from left to right gives the substituents at positions $3$ (ethyl) and $5$ (methyl).
- Numbering from right to left gives the substituents at positions $3$ (methyl) and $5$ (ethyl).

4. Apply the alphabetical rule: When two different numbering schemes give the same set of locants ($3, 5$), the lower number is assigned to the substituent that is cited first alphabetically. Since 'ethyl' comes before 'methyl', the ethyl group must get the lower number ($3$).

5. Formulate the name: Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is $3$-ethyl-$5$-methylheptane.

Answer: $3$-ethyl-$5$-methylheptane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two products X and Y are formed in the following reaction sequence.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} W \xrightarrow[\text{warm}]{\text{dil. HNO}_3 + \text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} X + Y$
The suitable method that can be used for the separation of products X and Y is :
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene with methyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation, which yields toluene (W).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3$

Nitration of toluene with a mixture of $\text{HNO}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields a mixture of ortho-nitrotoluene and para-nitrotoluene as the major products (X and Y).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{warm}]{\text{dil. HNO}_3 + \text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{o-nitrotoluene} + \text{p-nitrotoluene}$

The boiling point of o-nitrotoluene is $222^\circ\text{C}$ and that of p-nitrotoluene is $238^\circ\text{C}$. Since the difference in their boiling points is small, they are separated by fractional distillation.

Answer: Fractional distillation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The number of chlorine atoms present in the organic products X and Y of the following reactions, respectively, are :
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} X$
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} Y$
questions.solution:
Reaction 1 is an electrophilic aromatic substitution. Benzene reacts with excess chlorine in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ (a Lewis acid) to form hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6 + 6\text{HCl}$

The organic product X is hexachlorobenzene, which contains $6$ chlorine atoms.

Reaction 2 is a free radical addition reaction. Benzene reacts with chlorine in the presence of UV light to form benzene hexachloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$), also known as gammaxene or lindane.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$

The organic product Y is benzene hexachloride, which contains $6$ chlorine atoms.

Therefore, the number of chlorine atoms in both X and Y is $6$.

Answer: $6$ and $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In a qualitative analysis $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ is detected by appearance of precipitate of $\text{BiO(OH)(s)}$. Calculate pH when the following equilibrium exists at $298$ K :
$\text{BiO(OH)(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^{+}\text{(aq)} + \text{OH}^{-}\text{(aq)}$,
$K = 4 \times 10^{-10}$
(Given : $\log 2 = 0.3010$)
questions.solution:
The equilibrium reaction is given by:

$\text{BiO(OH)(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^{+}\text{(aq)} + \text{OH}^{-}\text{(aq)}$

The equilibrium constant expression is:

$K = [\text{BiO}^{+}][\text{OH}^{-}]$

Let the solubility of $\text{BiO(OH)}$ be $s$. Then $[\text{BiO}^{+}] = s$ and $[\text{OH}^{-}] = s$.

Substituting the values into the equilibrium expression:

$s^2 = 4 \times 10^{-10}$

$s = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$

Therefore, the concentration of hydroxide ions is:

$[\text{OH}^{-}] = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$

Calculating the pOH:

$\text{pOH} = -\log[\text{OH}^{-}] = -\log(2 \times 10^{-5}) = 5 - \log 2$

Given $\log 2 = 0.3010$:

$\text{pOH} = 5 - 0.3010 = 4.699$

The pH of the solution at $298 \text{ K}$ is:

$\text{pH} = 14 - \text{pOH} = 14 - 4.699 = 9.301$

Answer: $9.301$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At $298$ K, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of $X^{-}$ and $HX$, $K_b$ for $X^{-}$ is $10^{-10}$. What is the pH of this buffer solution ?
questions.solution:
Given $K_b$ for $X^{-} = 10^{-10}$.

For a conjugate acid-base pair at $298$ K, $K_a \times K_b = K_w = 10^{-14}$.

$K_a = \dfrac{10^{-14}}{10^{-10}} = 10^{-4}$

The $pK_a$ of the weak acid $HX$ is:

$pK_a = -\log(K_a) = -\log(10^{-4}) = 4$

Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer:

$\text{pH} = pK_a + \log \left( \dfrac{[X^{-}]}{[HX]} \right)$

Since the concentrations of $X^{-}$ and $HX$ are equal, $[X^{-}] = [HX]$.

$\text{pH} = 4 + \log(1) = 4 + 0 = 4$

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Phenolphthalein is used as an indicator for the titration of sodium hydroxide solution against a standard solution of oxalic acid. The colour change that is observed at an alkaline pH close to the equivalence point during this titration is :
questions.solution:
In the standardisation of sodium hydroxide using a standard solution of oxalic acid, oxalic acid (a primary standard) is taken in the conical flask and sodium hydroxide is taken in the burette.

Phenolphthalein is used as the indicator, which is colourless in an acidic medium and pink in an alkaline medium.

Initially, the solution in the conical flask contains oxalic acid, so it remains colourless.

As sodium hydroxide is added, the pH of the solution increases. At the equivalence point, the salt formed is sodium oxalate, which is a salt of a weak acid and a strong base. It undergoes anionic hydrolysis to give an alkaline solution.

At this alkaline pH (in the range of $8.2$ to $10.0$), the phenolphthalein indicator changes its colour to pink.

Thus, the observed colour change at the equivalence point is colourless to pink.

Answer: colourless to pink

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
options: Carbon has the ability to form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bond with itself.
$\text{ECl}_3\ (E = B\ \text{and}\ \text{Al})$ is a monomer when $E = B$ and a dimer when $E = Al$.
The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is $C  \gt  \gt  Si  \gt  Ge \approx Sn$.
questions.solution:
Carbon has a strong tendency to form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself, such as in alkenes and alkynes. Thus, the first statement is correct.

$\text{BCl}_3$ exists as a monomer because boron cannot expand its octet to form a dimer, whereas $\text{AlCl}_3$ exists as a dimer ($\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$) to complete its octet. Thus, the second statement is correct.

The catenation property depends on the element-element bond strength. The bond enthalpy decreases down the group, so the order of catenation is $C \gt \gt Si \gt Ge \approx Sn$. Thus, the third statement is correct.

Oxygen exhibits a $-2$ oxidation state in most of its compounds, but it also exhibits a $-1$ oxidation state in peroxides (e.g., $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$), a $-1/2$ oxidation state in superoxides (e.g., $\text{KO}_2$), and positive oxidation states when bonded to fluorine (e.g., $+2$ in $\text{OF}_2$ and $+1$ in $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$). Thus, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Answer: Oxygen exhibits only $-2$ oxidation state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
options: Nitrogen can form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself.
$\text{P}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3$ and $\text{As}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_3$ form $d\pi$-$d\pi$ bond with transition metals.
Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property.
Nitrogen can form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond with oxygen.
questions.solution:
Nitrogen and oxygen both belong to the second period of the periodic table.

The valence shell electronic configuration of nitrogen is $2s^{2} 2p^{3}$ and that of oxygen is $2s^{2} 2p^{4}$.

Since the principal quantum number is $n=2$ for both elements, they do not have vacant d-orbitals in their valence shells.

Therefore, nitrogen cannot form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds with oxygen. They can only form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds.

Statement (1) is correct as nitrogen forms $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself (e.g., in $N_{2}$).

Statement (2) is correct because phosphorus and arsenic have vacant d-orbitals and can act as $\pi$-acceptor ligands, forming $d\pi$-$d\pi$ back-bonds with the filled d-orbitals of transition metals.

Statement (3) is correct as phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony exhibit the property of catenation.

Thus, the incorrect statement is (4).

Answer: Nitrogen can form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond with oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a test tube containing a salt, a few drops of dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ was added, which gave colourless vapours having the smell of vinegar. The vapours turned the blue litmus paper red. Identify the correct anion from the following :
questions.solution:
When a salt containing the acetate anion ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-}$) is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) is formed.

$2\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$

Acetic acid vapours are colourless and have a characteristic smell of vinegar. Being acidic in nature, these vapours turn blue litmus paper red.

Sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) gives $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas which has a rotten egg smell.

Sulphate ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) does not react with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) gives $\text{CO}_2$ gas which is odourless.

Answer: Acetate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to :
options: increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component.
formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform.
stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.
questions.solution:
Chloroform ($CHCl_3$) and acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$) form a non-ideal solution showing a negative deviation from Raoult's law.

This is because the hydrogen atom of chloroform forms a hydrogen bond with the oxygen atom of acetone.

The formation of this intermolecular hydrogen bond makes the attractive forces between the unlike molecules stronger than the attractive forces between the like molecules.

As a result, the escaping tendency of the molecules from the liquid phase decreases, leading to a lower vapour pressure than expected from Raoult's law.

Answer: formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements :
A. The molality of $2.5$ g of ethanoic acid (Molar mass : $60$ g mol$^{-1}$) in $75$ g of benzene solution is $0.556$ m.
B. The molarity of a solution containing $5$ g of NaOH (molar mass : $40$ g mol$^{-1}$) in $450$ mL of solution is $0.278$ M at $298$ K.
C. Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water.
D. The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure.
E. For a binary mixture of A and B, the number of moles of A and B are $n_A$ and $n_B$ respectively. The mole fraction of B will be $x_B = \dfrac{n_A}{n_A + n_B}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A : Molality is given by the number of moles of solute divided by the mass of solvent in kg.
Moles of ethanoic acid $= \dfrac{2.5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{24}$ mol
Mass of benzene $= 75$ g $= 0.075$ kg
Molality $= \dfrac{1/24}{0.075} = \dfrac{1000}{24 \times 75} = \dfrac{1000}{1800} = \dfrac{5}{9} = 0.556$ m
Statement A is correct.

Statement B : Molarity is given by the number of moles of solute divided by the volume of solution in litres.
Moles of NaOH $= \dfrac{5}{40} = \dfrac{1}{8}$ mol
Volume of solution $= 450$ mL $= 0.45$ L
Molarity $= \dfrac{1/8}{0.45} = \dfrac{1000}{8 \times 450} = \dfrac{1000}{3600} = \dfrac{5}{18} = 0.278$ M
Statement B is correct.

Statement C : The solubility of gases (like oxygen) in water increases with a decrease in temperature. Therefore, cold water contains more dissolved oxygen, making aquatic species more comfortable.
Statement C is correct.

Statement D : According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the pressure of the gas. Thus, solubility decreases with a decrease in pressure.
Statement D is incorrect.

Statement E : The mole fraction of component B is the ratio of the number of moles of B to the total number of moles in the mixture.
$x_B = \dfrac{n_B}{n_A + n_B}$
Statement E is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements A, B, and C are correct.

Answer: A, B and C only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When $1$ dm$^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gas is passed over hot coke, the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes $1.4$ dm$^3$. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is :
questions.solution:
The reaction of carbon dioxide with hot coke is given by:

$\text{CO}_2(g) + \text{C}(s) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}(g)$

Initial volume of $\text{CO}_2 = 1$ dm$^3$

Let $x$ dm$^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ react with hot coke.

Volume of $\text{CO}_2$ remaining $= 1 - x$ dm$^3$

Volume of $\text{CO}$ formed $= 2x$ dm$^3$

Total volume of the gaseous mixture $= (1 - x) + 2x = 1 + x$ dm$^3$

Given that the total volume after the reaction is $1.4$ dm$^3$:

$1 + x = 1.4$

$x = 0.4$ dm$^3$

Volume of $\text{CO}_2$ remaining $= 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$ dm$^3$

Volume of $\text{CO}$ formed $= 2 \times 0.4 = 0.8$ dm$^3$

The composition of the gaseous mixture is $0.8$ dm$^3$ of CO and $0.6$ dm$^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$.

Answer: $0.8$ dm$^3$ of CO, $0.6$ dm$^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The number of hydrogen atoms present in $5.4$ g of urea is :
(Given : Molar mass of urea : $60$ g mol$^{-1}$, $N_A : 6.022 \times 10^{23}$ particles mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of urea is $NH_2CONH_2$.

Number of moles of urea $= \dfrac{5.4}{60} = 0.09$ mol.

One molecule of urea contains $4$ hydrogen atoms.

Number of moles of hydrogen atoms $= 4 \times 0.09 = 0.36$ mol.

Total number of hydrogen atoms $= 0.36 \times N_A = 0.36 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 2.16792 \times 10^{23} \approx 2.168 \times 10^{23}$.

Answer: $2.168 \times 10^{23}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A bulb is rated at $150$ watt, converting $8\%$ energy into light. If energy of one photon is $4.42 \times 10^{-19}$ J, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second ?
questions.solution:
Power of the bulb, $P = 150$ W

Energy converted into light per second, $E = 8\%$ of $150$ J

$E = \dfrac{8}{100} \times 150 = 12$ J

Energy of one photon, $E_p = 4.42 \times 10^{-19}$ J

Number of photons emitted per second, $n = \dfrac{E}{E_p}$

$n = \dfrac{12}{4.42 \times 10^{-19}}$

$n = 2.71 \times 10^{19}$

Answer: $2.71 \times 10^{19}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Quantum Numbers)List II (Orbital)
'n''l'
A.$2$$1$I. $3d$
B.$4$$0$II. $2p$
C.$5$$3$III. $4s$
D.$3$$2$IV. $5f$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The principal quantum number $n$ represents the shell, and the azimuthal quantum number $l$ represents the subshell.

For $l = 0$, the subshell is $s$.
For $l = 1$, the subshell is $p$.
For $l = 2$, the subshell is $d$.
For $l = 3$, the subshell is $f$.

A. $n = 2$, $l = 1$ corresponds to the $2p$ orbital. (A \rightarrow II)
B. $n = 4$, $l = 0$ corresponds to the $4s$ orbital. (B \rightarrow III)
C. $n = 5$, $l = 3$ corresponds to the $5f$ orbital. (C \rightarrow IV)
D. $n = 3$, $l = 2$ corresponds to the $3d$ orbital. (D \rightarrow I)

The correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

Answer: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction :
$2\text{A (g)} + \text{B (g)} \rightarrow 2\text{D (g)}$
$\Delta U^{\ominus} = -10$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^{\ominus} = -44$ J K$^{-1}$ at $298$ K.
Identify the correct option with $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at $298$ K.
(Given : $R = 8.31$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:

$\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$

The standard enthalpy change $\Delta H^{\ominus}$ is given by:

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = \Delta U^{\ominus} + \Delta n_g R T$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = -10 + (-1) \times (8.31 \times 10^{-3}) \times 298$

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = -10 - 2.47638 = -12.47638 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

The standard Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ is:

$\Delta G^{\ominus} = \Delta H^{\ominus} - T \Delta S^{\ominus}$

$\Delta G^{\ominus} = -12.47638 - 298 \times (-44 \times 10^{-3})$

$\Delta G^{\ominus} = -12.47638 + 13.112 = +0.63562 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Since $\Delta G^{\ominus} \gt 0$, the reaction is non-spontaneous.

Answer: $+0.63568$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, non-spontaneous

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At a certain temperature, $T$ (K), during a process, $500$ J is absorbed by the system and work of $200$ J is done by the system. Then, change in internal energy of the system is :
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta U = q + W$

Heat absorbed by the system, $q = +500$ J

Work done by the system, $W = -200$ J

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta U = 500 + (-200) = 300$ J

Answer: $300$ J

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ac circuit contains a resistance of $1$ k$\Omega$, a capacitor of $0.1\ \mu F$ and an inductor of $1$ mH connected in series. The resonance frequency of the circuit is approximately :
questions.solution:
Given $L = 1 \text{ mH} = 10^{-3} \text{ H}$ and $C = 0.1\ \mu\text{F} = 10^{-7} \text{ F}$.

The resonance frequency of a series RLC circuit is given by $f_r = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$.

Substituting the values:

$f_r = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-3} \times 10^{-7}}}$

$f_r = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-10}}}$

$f_r = \dfrac{10^5}{2\pi} \text{ Hz}$

$f_r = \dfrac{50}{\pi} \text{ kHz} \approx 15.9 \text{ kHz}$

Answer: $15.9$ kHz

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The peak value of an alternating current is $5$ A and frequency is $60$ Hz. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value ?
questions.solution:
The alternating current is given by $I = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$.

The time taken to reach the peak value from zero corresponds to a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

$\omega t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$2 \pi f t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$t = \dfrac{1}{4f}$

Given $f = 60$ Hz, we get:

$t = \dfrac{1}{4 \times 60} = \dfrac{1}{240}$ s.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{240}$ s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the energy of its electron is $-3.4$ eV. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately :
(Take $1$ eV $= 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J, $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}$ N m$^2$/C$^2$)
questions.solution:
The total energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom is given by $E = -\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{e^2}{2r}$

Substituting the given values:

$-3.4 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = -\dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{2r}$

$r = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{2 \times 3.4}$

$r = \dfrac{14.4 \times 10^{-10}}{6.8}$

$r \approx 2.117 \times 10^{-10}$ m

This is approximately $2.1 \times 10^{-10}$ m.

Answer: $2.1 \times 10^{-10}$ m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider two uncharged capacitors of equal capacitance $200$ pF. One of them is charged by a $100$ V supply and disconnected. Now this capacitor is connected to the uncharged capacitor. The amount of electrostatic energy lost in the process is :
questions.solution:
Initial energy of the charged capacitor is given by $U_i = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^2$.

When it is connected to an identical uncharged capacitor, the common potential becomes $V' = \dfrac{CV}{C+C} = \dfrac{V}{2}$.

Final energy of the system is $U_f = \dfrac{1}{2}(2C)V'^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(2C)\left(\dfrac{V}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}CV^2$.

Energy lost during the process is $\Delta U = U_i - U_f = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^2 - \dfrac{1}{4}CV^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}CV^2$.

Substituting the given values $C = 200 \times 10^{-12}$ F and $V = 100$ V:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 200 \times 10^{-12} \times (100)^2$

$\Delta U = 50 \times 10^{-12} \times 10^4 = 0.5 \times 10^{-6}$ J.

Answer: $0.5 \times 10^{-6}$ J

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Five capacitors of capacitances $C_1 = C_2 = C_3 = C_4 = 10\ \mu F$ and $C_5 = 2.5\ \mu F$ are connected as shown, along with a battery of $50$ V.

The equivalent capacitance and the charges on each capacitor respectively are :
options: $5\ \mu F$, $125\ \mu C$ on $C_1$ to $C_4$ and $25\ \mu C$ on $C_5$
questions.solution:
From the given circuit diagram, the capacitors $C_1, C_2, C_3$, and $C_4$ are connected in series. This series combination is connected in parallel with the capacitor $C_5$. The entire combination is connected across the $50\text{ V}$ battery.

Let $C_s$ be the equivalent capacitance of the series branch containing $C_1, C_2, C_3$, and $C_4$.
$\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} + \dfrac{1}{C_3} + \dfrac{1}{C_4}$
$\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{4}{10}\ \mu\text{F}^{-1}$
$C_s = 2.5\ \mu\text{F}$

The total equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ of the circuit is the sum of the parallel capacitances $C_s$ and $C_5$:
$C_{eq} = C_s + C_5 = 2.5\ \mu\text{F} + 2.5\ \mu\text{F} = 5\ \mu\text{F}$

The voltage across the series branch is equal to the battery voltage, $V = 50\text{ V}$.
The charge on the series combination is:
$Q_s = C_s \times V = 2.5\ \mu\text{F} \times 50\text{ V} = 125\ \mu\text{C}$
Since $C_1, C_2, C_3$, and $C_4$ are in series, they each carry the same charge $Q_s$.
Therefore, charge on $C_1, C_2, C_3, C_4 = 125\ \mu\text{C}$.

The voltage across capacitor $C_5$ is also $50\text{ V}$.
The charge on $C_5$ is:
$Q_5 = C_5 \times V = 2.5\ \mu\text{F} \times 50\text{ V} = 125\ \mu\text{C}$

Thus, the equivalent capacitance is $5\ \mu\text{F}$ and the charge on all capacitors is $125\ \mu\text{C}$.

Answer: $5\ \mu F$, $125\ \mu C$ on all capacitors
